question: Should Microsoft Teams permanently adopt the proposed `accounts`/`defaultAccount` model, including root-level inheritance and legacy-default compatibility, as its public multi-bot configuration contract?
rationale: The implementation appears technically sound, but accepting new public configuration, setup, credential-selection, and persisted-state upgrade semantics is a product and compatibility decision that automated review cannot make safely.

options.title: Sponsor the account contract
options.body: Approve the proposed model, refresh the branch against current main, rerun exact-head validation, and land it as the canonical Teams multi-account implementation.

options.title: Request a narrower contract
options.body: Keep the PR open but ask the author to reduce inheritance or setup/state scope before accepting a permanent public contract.

options.title: Decline core multi-account support
options.body: Close this PR while leaving the canonical feature issue available for a future maintainer-sponsored direction.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the account contract
recommendation.body: Approve the proposed model, refresh the branch against current main, rerun exact-head validation, and land it as the canonical Teams multi-account implementation.
